Tasting Counter - Twelve Seats 
We cook with the dark and a little fire. 
Ombra is a counter for twelve, hidden behind an unmarked door in the old quarter. One menu. One season. One fire at the centre of the room. 
Reserve a seat -> 
 Embers * Ash Butter * Night Herbs * Fermentation * Wild Orchard * Charred Citrus * Cellar Smoke * Tidewater * Old Grain * Candle Wax * Embers * Ash Butter * Night Herbs * Fermentation * Wild Orchard * Charred Citrus * Cellar Smoke * Tidewater * Old Grain * Candle Wax * 
01 - Concept 
A room held together by heat, by hands, by the quiet between courses. 
We do not write a menu. We listen to the week: to the market, the boats, the orchard outside town, and we cook what is most alive that night. The fire is the only constant. 
Service is slow on purpose. Twelve guests, one pass, one pace. You will meet the cooks, watch the embers fall, and stay for three hours without noticing. Fig. 01 - Vessel, raku, 2026 "The fire is older than the recipe. We only translate." 
- Elia Marchetti, Chef 
02 - Tasting 
Six movements, one evening, written that morning. 
Mise - week 47 
EUR245 per guest, six courses. Wine pairing EUR165, non-alcoholic EUR85. Service begins at 19:30, sharp. 
 I 
First Light of the orchard 
Quince, raw cream, bitter almond, a whisper of smoke from the morning's first coals. Cider - Asturias, 2022 
 II 
Tide after the storm 
Day-boat langoustine, fennel pollen, the brine of its own shell reduced to glass. Albarino - Rias Baixas, 2021 
 III 
The Ember kept overnight 
Heirloom beet buried in ash since dawn, aged sheep's butter, sourdough crust. Trousseau - Jura, 2020 
 IV 
An Animal, patiently 
Forty-day lamb shoulder cooked beside the fire, charred allium, fermented plum. Mencia - Bierzo, 2018 
 V 
Field, Burnt and cooled 
Toasted grain ice, hazelnut praline, a cold pour of single-estate olive oil. PX - Montilla, 1998 
 VI 
Last Word 
Bitter chocolate, fig leaf, salt from the cliffs at Llanes. Genever - house infusion 
03 - The Chef 
Elia Marchetti. A quiet cook, a patient room. 
"I learned to cook from my grandmother, who never owned a thermometer and never made the same dish twice." 
 1986 Born in Pollenzo, between vineyards and his grandmother's hearth. 
 2008 Stages at Mugaritz and Etxebarri. Learns the discipline of fire. 
 2014 Opens Ombra with twelve seats and no sign on the door. 
 2019 First star. Refuses to expand. Closes Sundays and Mondays. 
 2024 Second star. Same twelve seats. Same fire. 
04 - Sala 
Terracotta walls, one candle, oak older than the city. 
Materials 
Hand-troweled lime plaster in burnt sienna. Reclaimed oak beams from a 17th-century granary. Cast iron, smoked glass, raw linen. 
Light 
Two sources only: the hearth at the centre of the counter, and a single tall taper at each setting. The room is never brighter than the food. 
Sound 
A custom playlist by composer Luis Tinoco. Strings, breath, the long pause. No screens, no notifications, no announcements. 
05 - Reserve 
Twelve seats. Two seatings. One evening at a time. 
Bookings open the first Monday of each month for the following month. A deposit of EUR100 per guest secures your seat and is fully credited to your bill. 
Service
